subject: design-technology
source_note: Topic structure follows the Eduqas/WJEC A-Level Design and Technology specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships.

units.name: Technical Principles
units.blurb: Advanced knowledge across the seven content areas

units.name: Design & Make Project (NEA)
units.blurb: A sustained, iterative design and make project

topics.name: Designing & Innovation
topics.blurb: Iterative design, creativity, design theory and innovation

topics.name: Materials & Components
topics.blurb: Properties, working characteristics and selection of materials and components

topics.name: Processes
topics.blurb: Forming, combining and manufacturing processes and ICT in making

topics.name: Industrial & Commercial Practice
topics.blurb: Scales of production, quality and commercial manufacture

topics.name: Product Analysis & Systems
topics.blurb: Analysing products and applying systems thinking

topics.name: Human Responsibility
topics.blurb: Sustainability, ethics and values in design solutions

topics.name: Public Interaction: Marketing & Research
topics.blurb: Researching markets and the consumer interface with products

topics.name: Brief, Research & Specification
topics.blurb: Identifying an opportunity and writing a brief and specification

topics.name: Developing & Modelling
topics.blurb: Iterative development, modelling and design communication

topics.name: Testing & Evaluation
topics.blurb: Testing against the specification and evaluating outcomes

connections.why: The choice of materials and components determines which processes are appropriate
Analysing existing products informs innovative design thinking
Making processes scale up into industrial and commercial production
Sustainability and ethics shape responsible material and component choices
Market and user research drives innovative, viable design
Research methods feed directly into identifying a brief and specification
The brief and specification guide iterative development and modelling
Developed and modelled ideas are realised as a working prototype
The prototype is tested and evaluated against the specification
Evaluation feeds back into the iterative development loop
Material and component knowledge underpins prototype manufacture
Design theory and iterative method underpin the development stage
Understanding commercial manufacture informs realistic prototyping
